subject: Staff Orbit: weekly checkpoint for QBR prep and OKR sync
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-02-20T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Staff Orbit: weekly checkpoint for QBR prep and OKR sync

Team — sending a compact weekly checkpoint ahead of Friday's prep session. Goal is to surface wins, material risks, and asks that need leadership time during the QBR dry-run. TL;DR at top.

TL;DR
- Wins: 20% latency improvement on hosted API for 8k-token tails; early Dedicated pilot onboarding with Nimbus on track.
- Risks: one eval regression on code-completion prompts (measurable drop in pass@1); capacity contention forecast for late-March runway.
- Asks: (1) 30m slot Friday for slide approvals (see attached one-pager); (2) decide whether to increase Dedicated reserve by 2x for Nimbus pilot; (3) signoff on budget reallocation for SRE overtime in the run-up.

Wins (short)
- Serving/runtime: kernel autotuner deployed to prod A on Feb 16 — we measured a 20% median p99 token latency reduction on our heavy tail tests. Detailed breakdown in latency-trends.csv attached.
- Sales/Customer: Nimbus Analytics signed the mutual action plan (MAP) yesterday; kickoff scheduled for Mar 1. Their pilot will validate cold-start throughput at scale.
- Ops: Canary rollout policy stability improved; fewer automatic fallbacks (down from 4/day to ~0.7/day).

Risks (priority)
1) Quality regression: Research flagged a 6% drop in pass@1 for code-completion on one curated eval set after recent quantization settings. This is isolated to the 3.1-quant profile but is actionable. Root cause hypothesis: KV-cache rounding in the new kernel path.
2) Capacity runway: current Dedicated reservations plus forecasted Nimbus pilot puts peak-provisioning pressure on the SFO region during the week of Mar 20. If we don't add buffer capacity or enable overflow routing to us-west-2, we risk throttling at 95th percentile.
3) QBR narrative: we need a clear mitigation story for the regression and a plan showing how Dedicated customers won't be impacted.

Asks (explicit)
- LAURA: approve a 30-minute slot Friday 10:00–10:30 PT to sign off on the QBR one-pager and the mitigation slide. I attached a draft (QBR-one-pager.pdf).
- JONAS + MARISSA: confirm whether SRE OT budget can cover two 24-hour on-call shifts during Mar 15–25 (we estimate $9k). If not, we need to re-scope Nimbus pilot capacity.
- KARTHIK: quick estimate: what is the dollar impact to committed Dedicated if we bump up reserves by 100% for Nimbus? (need a high-level number for the QBR).

Notes on next steps
- I'll coordinate a dry-run deck update tonight and circulate a final one-pager morning of Friday. If Laura signs off, we'll lock slides and notify execs.

Attachments: [Attachment: QBR-one-pager.pdf (PDF, 480KB)], [Attachment: latency-trends.csv (CSV, 90KB)], [Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (XLSX, 240KB)]

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior PM, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-20T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staff Orbit: weekly checkpoint for QBR prep and OKR sync

Thanks — this is clear and tight. I'm good to approve a brief slot tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT; calendar invite sent. Two quick asks before the dry run: 

1) Put a one-slide "customer impact" summary that shows worst-case latency and the rollback path (we need a clear risk -> mitigation -> owner flow).
2) Marissa — please include the SRE cost delta as a single-line figure on slide 4 (Priyom: if you can get the OT estimate by noon, Laura will include).

On the regression: don't bury unknowns — include the current repro steps, scope (what models and quant profiles), and the proposed rollback trigger (e.g., >5% drop in pass@1 sustained for 24h). We will want to present a decision lane, not just a problem.

I'll review the attached one-pager tonight; Priyom, circle back with the updated slide before 12:00 PT so we can finalize.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Quick update on SRE capacity and cost:
- We ran numbers with Ops finance: adding two 24h on-call shifts for Mar 15–25 (to cover the Nimbus ramp) is ~$8.7k total (labor + surge slack). I penciled $9k in the notes to be conservative.
- If execs prefer not to expand the OT budget, we can alternatively throttle pilot concurrency (reduce per-customer reserved tokens) which would extend the validation timeline by ~2 weeks. That option keeps costs flat but risks slipping our timeline for production signoff.

I'll attach a short capacity delta spreadsheet to the deck. Priyom — sending the OT estimate to Laura by 12:00 PT.

-Marissa
Director, Production Ops
Redwood Inference
